notes: NCBI Bookshelf Pulmonary Sequestration was reread on 2026-08-27; the current StatPearls 2026 edition directly supports the defining tracheobronchial isolation, intralobar pleural relationship, systemic arterial supply, and pulmonary venous drainage.
The official USMLE Content Outline 2026 was inspected at Respiratory System p. 20 and explicitly lists pulmonary sequestration under congenital disorders.
A 2026 PubMed-indexed Respiratory Investigation study provides contemporary confirmation that intralobar pulmonary sequestration involves abnormal lung with systemic arterial supply.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.defining_anatomy: NCBI defines pulmonary sequestration as nonfunctioning dysplastic lung tissue lacking normal communication with the tracheobronchial tree and receiving anomalous systemic vascular supply.
claim_audit.intralobar_pleura: NCBI states that intralobar sequestration is located within the visceral pleura of the functioning lung, matching the vignette.
claim_audit.arterial_supply: NCBI states that systemic arterial supply most commonly arises from the descending thoracic aorta, while recognizing less common systemic sources; the lead therefore appropriately asks for the most likely pattern rather than an absolute.
claim_audit.venous_drainage: NCBI states that intralobar sequestration typically drains to pulmonary veins, whereas extralobar sequestration has separate pleura and systemic venous drainage, commonly via azygos/hemiazygos pathways.
claim_audit.distractor_1: Pulmonary arterial inflow with pulmonary venous drainage represents normal pulmonary perfusion and lacks the defining systemic arterial supply of a sequestration.
claim_audit.distractor_2: Descending-aortic inflow with azygos/hemiazygos drainage is more consistent with extralobar sequestration; the vignette explicitly places the lesion within the same visceral pleura as adjacent lung.
claim_audit.distractor_3: Pulmonary arterial inflow does not match the defining systemic arterial supply of pulmonary sequestration, and systemic venous drainage does not match the usual intralobar pattern.
claim_audit.distractor_4: Bronchial-arterial inflow with direct SVC drainage is not the typical vascular configuration of intralobar sequestration and is not supported by the lesion's classic anatomy.
claim_audit.blueprint_claim: The official USMLE 2026 Content Outline explicitly includes pulmonary sequestration under Respiratory System congenital disorders.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Recurrent infection in the same lower-lobe region plus an abnormal lung segment without normal tracheobronchial communication indicates sequestration. Sharing the visceral pleura with adjacent lung identifies the intralobar form. From that classification, the expected vascular pattern is anomalous systemic arterial inflow, most commonly from the descending thoracic aorta, with pulmonary venous drainage.
adversarial_second_pass.intralobar_vs_extralobar_challenge: The pleural clue is decisive: intralobar lesions share visceral pleura with normal lung; extralobar lesions have a separate pleural covering. This makes the systemic-venous distractor noncompetitive.
adversarial_second_pass.vascular_variation_challenge: Pulmonary sequestration can receive systemic arterial blood from vessels other than the descending thoracic aorta and venous variants exist. The item uses 'most likely,' so the canonical common pattern remains uniquely best without falsely claiming universality.
adversarial_second_pass.normal_circulation_challenge: Pulmonary artery to pulmonary vein is normal lung circulation, not sequestration, because the defining abnormality is systemic arterial supply.
adversarial_second_pass.developmental_precision_challenge: The item tests established anatomic classification and does not depend on a disputed single embryologic mechanism or accessory-bud theory.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: Options are parallel arterial-supply/venous-drainage pairs. The correct answer is not uniquely longer, more specific in style, or the only option using terminology from the stem.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The item avoids unsupported percentages and does not require a fixed vessel origin or drainage route in every case; 'most likely' accommodates documented anatomic variation.
